fields.name: name

fields.notes: Email Reminders tab field (create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md, 15-row roster). fields.name: reminder-type
fields.label: Reminder Type
fields.sourceQuote: Select the type that this email reminder applies to. Reminder Type serves as a category for the rules that apply to that type as well as the action that the reminders are activated upon:
fields.notes: Email Reminders tab field. COLLIDES with rule_reminder_type below - same label on both rosters. See contradiction node 'reminder-type-option-list-and-definition' - this file's list and definitions genuinely disagree with the Rules-tab roster's list. 'Only the rules with this reminder type will appear in the next field' (Reminder Rule) ties this field's selection to filtering the Reminder Rule field's options - see dependencyCandidate.

fields.name: reminder-rule
fields.label: Reminder Rule
fields.sourceQuote: Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.
fields.notes: Selects among rules created on the Rules tab (the rule_name object), filtered by the Reminder Type selected above; not enumerable as a static value set - its population is dynamic (whatever rules exist for the chosen type, including the 2 system-supplied default rules named on Pre-Defined Rules). 'The Email Reminder Rules section of this tool is used to create any new rules.' Hard ordering: a rule must exist before a reminder can select one here - see dependencyCandidate rule-precedes-reminder. REPAIRED IN ROSTER ASSEMBLY (refuter-1, the one repair on this page): fieldType was 'dropdown'; changed to 'unknown'. Grounds: the only description the corpus gives is 'Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.' - a HELPER, and the same file treats 'Helper pane' as a distinct widget for Email Subject / Email Message. The corpus nowhere calls this control a dropdown, a list or a modal, so 'dropdown' asserted a widget the source does not describe and would send a Chromium driver hunting for a select element. The tables lens already had 'unknown'. validValues stays [] - the population is dynamic (tenant-created rules filtered by Reminder Type). SEED POPULATION, for the merger to wire as a value set, NOT as the field's complete option list: pre-defined-rules-220a1fe7.md enumerates exactly two system-supplied rules, 'Overdue Payment Request Approvals' and 'Overdue Payment Vendor Approvals', under the quote 'The pre-defined rules are as follows:' (grep -F verified). No configuration surface for those two pre-defined rules is documented anywhere - whether they can be edited, copied or deleted is UNDETERMINED.

fields.name: frequency
fields.label: Frequency
fields.sourceQuote: Select how often you want this email to be sent once a rule is violated:
fields.notes: Email Reminders tab field. Controls conditional visibility of Number of Days (only if Every x days) and Specific days (only if Specific days of the month) - see dependencyCandidates. 'Once condition is met' carries a documented flag-reset caveat: flags are cleared every 60 days for performance reasons, so a once-only reminder can effectively repeat every 60 days unless the rule itself adds a time- or status-based guard condition.

fields.name: number-of-days
fields.label: Number of Days
fields.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Every x days in the Frequency field.
fields.notes: Conditionally visible: only if Frequency = 'Every x days'. 'Enter the number of days since the last email reminder that this email is to be sent.' Behavior note: 'An email will be sent initially once the condition is met, then every “x days” as specified.'

fields.name: specific-days
fields.label: Specific days
fields.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month in the Frequency field.
fields.notes: Conditionally visible: only if Frequency = 'Specific days of the month'. 'Enter a valid integer between 1 and 31. Use > for the last day of the month.' Example: '10, 20, > in the field would run the reminder on the 10th, 20th, and the last day of the month.' See compressedRange 'valid integer between 1 and 31'.

fields.name: display-as-from

fields.name: email-subject
fields.label: Email Subject

fields.name: email-message
fields.label: Email Message

The Email Reminders tab's New opens the reminder editor ('Choose New to open the Email Reminder window.', create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md) while the Rules tab's New opens the rule wizard ('The New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page appears.') and carries a role gate the reminder side does not: 'If they do not have permissions, then the New button will not appear.' (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md, grep -F -c = 1). The graph's own precedent splits per object elsewhere (page.audit-rules carries CustomRuleModifyButton and ValidationRuleModifyButton separately), and a tab-scoped Chromium driver would need two targets. NOT SPLIT HERE because a record created during Repair never faces the adversarial refuter; the single emitted record's notes quote and attribute both tab behaviours and the rule-side gate. PUNCTUATION WARNING for whoever executes this: the rule-side step reads 'Choose New' with no trailing period, so 'Choose New.' returns 0 against create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md.

Two distinct Modify controls on two objects. Reminder side: 'Choose Modify to open the Email Reminder window.' (edit-email-reminders-2a2638ad.md) with the read-only gate 'Group administrators can only edit email reminders if given "create" rights from the configuration checklist of the Invoice Configuration administrator.' Rule side: 'Select the rule to edit, and then choose Modify.' (edit-reminder-rules-8f2edae9.md, grep -F -c = 1), which opens the two-step wizard instead of the window. verifyNotes:
ASSEMBLY RESULT: 26 inputs in (25 keep + 1 repair), 26 records out, 0 dropped, 0 split. Every record was pulled PROGRAMMATICALLY out of extract-email-reminders-procedure.json with python3 - no quote was retyped by hand. Both refuters gave verbatimVariantIndex 0 on all 26 candidates and agreed with each other; variant 0 is the procedures-and-controls record in every case, and the procedures lens is also the only lens carrying all 26 names (the tables lens has 18, all underscore-spelled; the crosscut lens emitted zero fields, correctly). I re-verified all 26 sourceQuotes myself with grep -F -c against the cited file: ALL 26 RETURNED EXACTLY 1. Zero misses, zero wrong-directory paths, no record carries the CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix that broke an earlier drop pass.

THE ONE REPAIR - reminder-rule. Defect named by refuter-1: fieldType 'dropdown' asserted a widget the corpus never names. Fixed to 'unknown' (the value the tables lens already had). The only description in the source is 'Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.' - a HELPER - and the same file treats 'Helper pane' as a separate widget for Email Subject / Email Message. A Chromium driver told 'dropdown' would hunt for a select element that the documentation does not describe. sourceQuote, sourceFile, label, validValues ([] - the population is dynamic) and fromRawHtmlTable are unchanged and the quote re-verifies at 1. The repair is described in the record's own notes, along with the secondary item refuter-1 asked for: the two system-supplied seed rules from pre-defined-rules-220a1fe7.md are recorded there as a SEED population for the merger to wire as a value set, explicitly NOT as the field's complete option list.

NOTHING WAS SPLIT, ON PURPOSE. Refuter-2 finding 9 is right that New, Modify and Remove are each attested on BOTH tabs and that the graph's own precedent elsewhere (page.audit-rules CustomRuleModifyButton vs ValidationRuleModifyButton) splits per object. But records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter, and mis-assignment is exactly what grep cannot catch, so all three stay as single best-grounded records whose notes already quote and attribute both tab behaviours. The three splits are reported in splitsProposed for the human instead. Rule-side quotes for them are grep -F verified and available: 'If they do not have permissions, then the New button will not appear.' (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md, 1 hit), 'Select the rule to edit, and then choose Modify.' (edit-reminder-rules-8f2edae9.md, 1 hit), 'Select the rule to delete, and then choose Remove.' (delete-reminder-rules-ab4f8d33.md, 1 hit).
